title: The normal way of creating MeshLibraries doesn't set '_editor_source_scene' meta
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in master, 4.4.dev7 and 3.6.1. Issue probably happens since forever.

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev7 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - GeForce 920M - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-5500U CPU @ 2.40GHz (4 threads)

### Issue description

Have you ever wanted to update a MeshLibrary after editing the scene that was used to build said MeshLibrary? I would always create an entirely new MeshLib (with a new name, because issues) and replace the existing one.

Well, it turns out that MeshLib has that functionality already. Upon editing the MeshLibrary (making it appear in the Inspector dock), there is an option in the spatial bar menu (above 3d viewport) called "Update from Scene". However, it's probably greyed out. Why? Because a MeshLib meta variable '_editor_source_scene' doesn't exist.

The usual way to create a MeshLibrary (Scene > Export As > MeshLibrary) calls 'update_library_file' from mesh_library_editor_plugin.cpp, which calls _import_scene. However, this internal method doesn't set that meta variable. The next method in the file, '_import_scene_cbk', does.

'_import_scene_cbk' is only called when you use the "Import from Scene" Meshlib spatial bar menu options. Likely not the common way to create a Meshlib, and definitely not the way the docs and virtually every tutorial shows.

### Steps to reproduce

1) Follow the usual step by step to create a MeshLibrary ([as per docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/using_gridmaps.html));
2) Edit (double click) the newly created MeshLibrary, so that it appears in the Inspector Dock. The spatial menu, above 3d viewport, should also appear;
3) Notice the spatial menu option "Update from Scene" is greyed out.

The "unusual" way allows that option to be used:
1) Create a new empty MeshLibrary and edit it;
2) Use any of the "Import from Scene" options;
3) Now, the option "Update from Scene" should be editable. To check that it can update, edit the source scene (change a mesh Resource, a Transform etc.), **then save scene**, then edit the Meshlib and click "Update from Scene". The Meshlib should be updated.
Any GridMap using that MeshLibrary should also have their painted cells updated.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Probably not needed? Any MeshLib created as per docs suffers from this.
